During her time at Brown, she played a pivotal role in managing the business operations for one of the Ivy League's largest athletics programs. Over the past three years, Kincade spearheaded numerous strategic initiatives within Brown's business office, including implementing zero-based budgeting, and the comprehensive oversight of financial planning, forecasting, and reporting. Her collaborative approach helped streamline financial processes across 34 varsity sports and additional recreational units, ensuring a transparent and efficient resource management system.\u003Cbr />\r\n\u003Cbr />\r\n\"First, I would like to thank \u003Cem>\u003Ca href=\"https://dartmouthsports.com/sports/athletics/roster/coaches/mike-harrity/9982\">Mike Harrity\u003C/a>\u003C/em> and Gregg DiNardo for extending this wonderful opportunity to be a part of the Dartmouth team,\" said Kincade. \"Dartmouth, and Dartmouth Athletics, have always been a place that I hold great admiration for growing up in the state. The level of growth and potential, coupled with the campus support for athletics, is something I am beyond excited about and grateful to be a part of.\"\u003Cbr />\r\n\u003Cbr />\r\n\"New Hampshire is my home,\" Kincade continued. \"Throughout my career progression, I have worked to this opportunity where I can now apply all of those skills back to a place, and a community, that means the world to me. I cannot wait to hit the ground running in the continual collaboration of building the best experience for all Dartmouth student-athletes, both as a Sport Administrator and a CFO.\"\u003Cbr />\r\n\u003Cbr />\r\nIn her new role at Dartmouth, Kincade will oversee all financial functions within the department, including budgeting, forecasting, financial reporting, and long-term fiscal planning. With collegiate athletics facing an era of significant change, Kincade's strategic leadership will be instrumental in ensuring the department's fiscal health and sustainability. She will work closely with coaches, administrators, and external partners to allocate resources efficiently and effectively, ensuring Dartmouth's student-athletes and programs have the necessary support to thrive.\u003Cbr />\r\n\u003Cbr />\r\n \"We are thrilled to welcome Julia Kincade to Dartmouth Athletics,\" said Gregg DiNardo, Deputy Athletics Director for Business Strategy and Operations. \"Her depth of experience in financial management, and her innovative approach to budgeting and resource allocation, will be critical as we navigate the evolving landscape of college athletics. Julia's expertise will not only strengthen our financial operations but also enhance our ability to support the successes of our student-athletes on and off the field.\"\u003Cbr />\r\n\u003Cbr />\r\nThroughout her career, Kincade has demonstrated a commitment to fiscal responsibility and operational excellence. At Brown, she was responsible for overseeing the processing and reporting of all financial transactions, developing and managing the annual operating budget, and compiling the Equity in Athletics Disclosure Act (EADA) and NCAA reports in partnership with a third-party audit firm. Her focus on transparency and precision in financial reporting earned her the respect of colleagues across the Ivy League and beyond.\u003Cbr />\r\n\u003Cbr />\r\nKincade's leadership extended beyond financial operations. She served as a sport administrator for multiple teams, including men's and women's swimming and diving, field hockey, men's and women's tennis, and sailing, providing administrative support and fostering a strong connection between the athletics department and student-athletes. Additionally, her involvement on Brown University's Title IX hearing panel demonstrated her commitment to equity and inclusion in collegiate athletics.\u003Cbr />\r\n\u003Cbr />\r\nThe Senior Associate Athletics Director for Finance & Administration/CFO position is a vital role within the Dartmouth Athletics Department, especially in today's rapidly evolving athletic environment. The ongoing deregulation of collegiate sports has placed a heightened emphasis on sound financial management. Ensuring that resources are allocated efficiently is critical to maintaining Dartmouth's competitive edge while upholding the department's commitment to providing a first-class experience for its student-athletes. Kincade's experience with long-term budgeting, forecasting, and financial reporting uniquely positions her to lead Dartmouth Athletics through this transformative period.\u003Cbr />\r\n\u003Cbr />\r\nAs a New Hampshire native, Kincade is thrilled to return to her home state with her husband Chad. \u003Cbr />\r\n\u003Cbr />\r\n\"Coming back to New Hampshire and joining Dartmouth feels like a homecoming for me,\" she shared. \"I'm excited to work alongside an incredible team and help further Dartmouth's tradition of excellence. I look forward to contributing to the success of our student-athletes and ensuring that Dartmouth Athletics remains a leader in both athletic and academic achievement.\"\u003Cbr />\r\n\u003Cbr />\r\nKincade's local roots, combined with her impressive professional experience, make Julia a natural fit for Dartmouth and the broader Hanover community. As Kincade transitions into her new role, she will leverage her expertise to continue Dartmouth's legacy of athletic success, while supporting the holistic development of its student-athletes.\u003Cbr dir=\"ltr\">Dartmouth Athletics proudly announces the hiring of Mallory Poole as Associate Athletics Director for Sports Administration, a newly created role designed to further enhance the level of administrative support to our coaches and varsity programs. After a national search, Poole emerged as the perfect addition to help guide Dartmouth's sport administration team into a new era of success and innovation. \u003Cbr />\r\n\u003Cbr />\r\n“During our national search, Mallory stood out from an exceptional group of finalists through her appreciation for Dartmouth’s distinctions, thoughtful approach to leadership, proven ability to navigate complex challenges with compassion and her clear vision for developing competitive programs,” said Mike Harrity, Haldeman Family Director of Athletics and Recreation. “We are thrilled to welcome Mallory back to Hanover and know she’ll make an immediate and lasting impact.”\u003Cbr />\r\n\u003Cbr />\r\nPoole brings to Dartmouth an exceptional blend of experience and passion. She has honed her leadership skills through various impactful roles in collegiate athletics, including as an assistant coach for Dartmouth women’s lacrosse during the 2008-09 season and most recently at the University of Nevada, Las Vegas (UNLV). There, she served as the Associate Athletics Director for Student-Athlete Wellness and Development and Senior Woman Administrator, where she played a crucial role on the executive leadership team. Her achievements included overseeing key wellness initiatives, stewarding significant endowments to advance women’s sports and crafting leadership and career development programs to prepare student-athletes for life beyond college sports. Her background also encompasses a strong emphasis on fostering inclusive environments, having chaired diversity equity, and inclusion efforts that left a lasting impact on department culture.\u003Cbr />\r\n\u003Cbr />\r\n\"Starting my professional journey with Dartmouth as a young lacrosse coach, and now returning at this stage in my career, is both meaningful and rewarding,” said Poole. “It became clear early on in my conversations that there is great momentum building in Hanover. The direction that Mike Harrity has been leading the department is refreshing, and I am honored to have the opportunity to contribute to the team's efforts. \u003Cbr />\r\n\u003Cbr />\r\nAs I have moved through my career, I have come to appreciate more and more what it means to work alongside quality people and how critical it is to have a strong alignment of values and leadership philosophies. I am grateful to have been connected to (Senior Deputy Athletics Director) Kristine Fowler over the years and then through this process, to have met Taurian Houston and several others in the department, all of whom are committed to providing an elite student experience at Dartmouth. I look forward to building upon the culture of excellence that is already in place as I strive to support our student-athletes and coaches in achieving their academic, athletic, and personal aspirations at the highest level. Dartmouth College is a special place with special people and I am energized and inspired to rejoin the staff.\"\u003Cbr />\r\n\u003Cbr />\r\nAs the Associate Athletics Director for Sports Administration at Dartmouth, Poole will offer strategic oversight and daily support to head coaches and the sport administration team, collaborating with the Athletics and Recreation Leadership Team to develop and implement innovative resources that enhance the effectiveness and efficiency of managing sport programs. By helping create a framework for professional development and streamlining sport administration processes, she aims to empower coaches and administrators alike. Poole will also directly supervise a portfolio of sports, working closely with head coaches to foster a culture of continuous improvement and competitiveness.\u003Cbr />\r\n\u003Cbr />\r\n“This new role of Associate Athletics Director for Sports Administration is crucial in shaping the future of our athletic programs,” said Taurian Houston, Executive Associate Athletics Director for Administration. “Mallory’s collaborative leadership style and commitment to excellence will ensure that our sport administrators and coaches are equipped to provide the best possible experience for our student-athletes. Her vision and strategic thinking align perfectly with our department’s goals and priorities.”\u003Cbr />\r\n\u003Cbr />\r\nDartmouth Athletics remains committed to supporting and developing student-athletes in a comprehensive and inclusive environment. Poole’s addition signifies a strengthened commitment to this mission, and her strategic guidance is anticipated to drive the department to even greater heights.\u003Cbr
